name: Valais
summary: Switzerland's largest wine region, on steep and sunny slopes. Pinot Noir and Chasselas, sold as Fendant, lead the plantings, beside local grapes such as Petite Arvine and Cornalin.
label_note: "AOC Valais" must appear in full on the main label. Grand Cru may only be used with the name of its commune or region; "Grand Cru Valais" is not allowed.

grapes.name: Pinot Noir
grapes.local_note: The base of Dôle, alone or blended with Gamay.

appellations.name: Valais
appellations.note: Cantonal AOC for grapes harvested and vinified in Valais.

appellations.name: Grand Cru
appellations.note: Communal or regional designation for AOC Valais wines from listed grapes, set by each commune's own regulation.

appellations.name: Vin des Glaciers
appellations.note: AOC white from the Sierre district, aged at least fifteen years in larch casks in the Val d'Anniviers.

name: Vaud
summary: Switzerland's second largest wine canton and the only one where white grapes lead. Chasselas covers more than half the vineyard, across regions such as Chablais, Lavaux and La Côte.
label_note: A Vaud AOC white with no grape named must be at least 90% Chasselas; a single named grape must make up at least 85% of the wine.

grapes.name: Chasselas
grapes.local_note: May be sold under the traditional name Dorin.

appellations.name: Vaud
appellations.note: Cantonal AOC for grapes harvested in the canton.

appellations.name: Chablais
appellations.note: Regional AOC: the wine communes of the Aigle district.

appellations.name: Lavaux
appellations.note: Regional AOC: the wine communes of the Lavaux-Oron and Riviera-Pays-d'Enhaut districts plus Lausanne.

appellations.name: La Côte
appellations.note: Regional AOC: the wine communes of the Ouest lausannois, Nyon and Morges districts, with four exceptions.

appellations.name: Côtes-de-l'Orbe
appellations.note: Regional AOC of twenty listed communes.

appellations.name: Bonvillars
appellations.note: Regional AOC of eight listed communes.

appellations.name: Vully
appellations.note: Regional AOC shared with Fribourg (Vully-les-Lacs and Mont-Vully).

appellations.name: Dézaley Grand cru
appellations.note: Delimited part of Puidoux, inside Lavaux.

appellations.name: Dézaley-Marsens Grand cru
appellations.note: Part of Puidoux north of the Route de la Corniche.

appellations.name: Calamin Grand cru
appellations.note: Part of the former commune of Epesses south of the Route de la Corniche.

name: Lavaux
summary: A regional appellation within Vaud covering the terraced vineyards east of Lausanne, listed by UNESCO in 2007. It contains the Dézaley and Calamin Grand Cru appellations.
label_note: Wines from Dézaley or Calamin may also use the Lavaux appellation. Blending with other wines (coupage) is not allowed for AOC Lavaux.

appellations.name: Lavaux
appellations.note: Regional AOC within Vaud.

appellations.name: Dézaley Grand cru
appellations.note: Delimited part of Puidoux; may carry only the commune name Puidoux.

appellations.name: Dézaley-Marsens Grand cru
appellations.note: Part of Puidoux north of the Route de la Corniche.

appellations.name: Calamin Grand cru
appellations.note: Part of the former commune of Epesses; may carry only the name Epesses.

name: Genève
summary: Vineyards around the city that continue over the border into France. Gamay is the most planted grape, just ahead of Chasselas, with Pinot Noir, Gamaret and Chardonnay next.
label_note: A commune or hamlet name may name an AOC Premier Cru only with an added term such as "Côte de" or "Coteau de". "Perlan" may appear on a still Chasselas.

appellations.name: Genève
appellations.note: Cantonal AOC; includes Challex, Ferney-Voltaire and parts of five other French communes.

appellations.name: Premier Cru
appellations.note: Category of AOC for plots delimited on cantonal plans; the individual names are not listed in the regulation.

name: Ticino
summary: Switzerland's wine region south of the Alps. Merlot covers about three quarters of the vineyard, and reds dominate; Merlot is also made as a white, known as Merlot bianco.
label_note: A grape named on a DOC Ticino label must make up at least 90% of the wine; blends are sold as Rosso, Bianco or Rosato del Ticino.

grapes.name: Merlot
grapes.local_note: Also vinified as a white, Merlot bianco.

appellations.name: Ticino
appellations.note: Cantonal DOC; grapes from Ticino and the Mesolcina.

appellations.name: Rosso del Ticino
appellations.note: DOC term for a blend of red grapes.

appellations.name: Bianco del Ticino
appellations.note: DOC term for a blend of white grapes.

appellations.name: Rosato del Ticino
appellations.note: DOC term for a rosé blend.

name: Neuchâtel
summary: A single cantonal AOC around Lake Neuchâtel. Pinot Noir and Chasselas are the main grapes, and the Non filtré, an unfiltered young Chasselas, is a local speciality.
label_note: Pinot Noir must contain at least 95% Pinot Noir. Non filtré is an unfiltered Chasselas released no earlier than the third Wednesday of January after harvest.

grapes.name: Chasselas
grapes.local_note: Also bottled unfiltered as Non filtré.

appellations.name: Neuchâtel
appellations.note: Cantonal AOC bounded by the canton's political limits.

appellations.name: Grand Cru
appellations.note: Regulated by the Neuchâtel wine interprofession; only still Chardonnay, Chasselas and red Pinot Noir.

name: Graubünden
summary: Vineyards along the Rhine from Bonaduz to Fläsch, including the Bündner Herrschaft villages. Pinot Noir, called Blauburgunder here, covers about two thirds of the area, in a mild climate shaped by the foehn.
label_note: A commune name may be added when at least 60% of the wine comes from that commune; a vineyard site name requires 100%.

appellations.name: Graubünden
appellations.note: Cantonal AOC (also KUB Graubünden, DOC Grigioni).

appellations.name: Graubünden Misox
appellations.note: Regional AOC for wines from the Misox (Mesolcina).
